summary: Modular monolith: React (Vite SPA) (web) on Go 1.27 (net/http + chi) with Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — West Europe (Netherlands), hosted on Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) — West Europe (Netherlands). Estimated $459-2388/month.

frontend.justification: Web: React (Vite SPA) — Rich interactive app screens; team already writes typescript for the UI; good performance (priority 5/5); good scalability (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Vue 3: smaller hiring pool and component ecosystem than React.

Learning curve 3/5 for a senior team (team.experience). React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Next.js: server runtime needed for SSR; more moving parts than a static site.

tradeoffs: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO
frontend.contrast: React (Vite SPA) (web) rather than Vue 3 (Vite SPA). React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Trade-off accepted: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO.

backend.justification: Team already writes go for the API; native WebSocket support; good performance (priority 5/5); good scalability (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Go 1.27 (net/http + chi) is stronger on: good performance (priority 5/5) (priorities.performance); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 0.8 points behind. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS: more boilerplate than Express.

Team lists go, typescript but this needs csharp (team.languages). Go 1.27 (net/http + chi) is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 10.0 points behind. Known limit of .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core: smaller open-source hosting choice outside Azure.

tradeoffs: More hand-written code than batteries-included frameworks

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: low
confidence.basis: stability 0.59 (sensitive) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 0.8 over the runner-up (near-tie).

backend.contrast: Go 1.27 (net/http + chi) rather than Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript). Go 1.27 (net/http + chi) is stronger on: good performance (priority 5/5) (priorities.performance); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Trade-off accepted: More hand-written code than batteries-included frameworks.

database.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 — West Europe (Netherlands)
database.justification: Strict ACID transactions for payments and the records they change; row-level security enforces tenant isolation in the database; handles write-heavy load; good maintainability (priority 4/5); good performance (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 3.2 points behind. Known limit of Azure SQL Database: licence cost outside Azure SQL; Windows-centric tooling.

Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 6.8 points behind. Known limit of Supabase Postgres: free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity; production needs Pro.

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 3.2 over the runner-up.

database.contrast: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 rather than Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose). Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Trade-off accepted: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions.

what_would_change.new_choice: No single-field edit among the probed priorities, requirements, numbers and constraints changes this choice (the managed provider still follows the hosting choice).

hosting.choice: Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) — West Europe (Netherlands)
hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (managed_cloud (no servers to patch)). Good maintainability (priority 4/5); good performance (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Google Cloud Run: cold starts unless min instances are paid for.

Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 4.0 points behind. Known limit of Azure Container Apps: more moving parts than App Service for a single web app.
Excluded: self-managed infrastructure, but deployment_model is managed_cloud (infrastructure.deployment_model).

tradeoffs: Less control than containers for unusual runtimes

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 0.91 (robust) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 2.4 over the runner-up.

Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Trade-off accepted: Less control than containers for unusual runtimes.

what_would_change.new_choice: AWS Elastic Beanstalk (managed platform on EC2) — eu-central-1 (Frankfurt)

supporting.choice: Keycloak 26 (container next to the API) with Google/GitHub/Microsoft OAuth
supporting.justification: social login on a self-hosted identity server: Go has no batteries-included auth framework, so Keycloak handles passwords, MFA and social providers and keeps identities in-region.

alternatives.why_not: extra monthly cost per active user and identity data outside your region
security-sensitive code the team would have to maintain

supporting.justification: Uploads (images, documents) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: bloats backups and costs more per GB
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside AZURE

supporting.choice: Yjs CRDT documents + Hocuspocus WebSocket server
supporting.justification: Many people edit the same board at once: CRDTs merge concurrent edits without conflicts and broadcast cursors/presence (awareness); Hocuspocus persists document updates to the database.

alternatives.why_not: fastest to start but per-room pricing and board data held by a third party
last-write-wins loses concurrent edits

tradeoffs: Stateful socket servers need sticky routing or a Redis pub/sub backplane when scaled out

supporting.choice: Azure Managed Redis in West Europe (Netherlands)
supporting.justification: Cache and pub/sub layer: ~5,000 concurrent users; pub/sub backplane so WebSocket messages reach users on every instance; performance priority 5.

alternatives.why_not: now source-available (RSALv2/SSPL); Valkey keeps the BSD licence
being retired (Sept 2028); Azure Managed Redis is the replacement

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor

supporting.choice: Azure Service Bus in West Europe (Netherlands)
supporting.justification: Background work: payment webhooks and ledger postings processed idempotently with retries; absorbs write bursts.

alternatives.why_not: slow responses and lost work when a call fails

supporting.choice: Stripe (Checkout) — Stripe Billing with per-seat subscription quantities
supporting.justification: Hosted checkout keeps card data off your servers (PCI DSS SAQ A scope when fully outsourced). Payment confirmation is trusted only from signed server-side webhooks.

alternatives.why_not: handles global tax but higher fees and less control
enterprise pricing/onboarding for this size

tradeoffs: Per-transaction fees (~2% domestic cards) are charged on revenue, not in the infrastructure band

supporting.justification: Caches public pages and static assets near users; only public, non-personal content is cached at the edge.

alternatives.why_not: every asset request hits the origin; slower for distant users

alternatives.choice: Cloudflare (free plan) in front of Azure
alternatives.why_not: cheaper for a small site, but a second vendor for DNS/TLS and outside the Azure contract

tradeoffs: Front Door Standard has a $35/month base fee before requests and egress

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances); free minutes cover a team of 5.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in West Europe (Netherlands)
supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider in West Europe (Netherlands); alerts on error rate and latency against the 100 ms p95 target.

alternatives.why_not: extra vendor; add later for richer error grouping

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Tenant isolation: tenant_id on every row + database row-level security
supporting.justification: Several customer organisations share the system: every query is scoped by tenant, enforced in the database so one bug cannot leak another team's boards.

alternatives.why_not: strong isolation but heavy operations for thousands of small teams

tradeoffs: Every new table needs a policy

assumptions: Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances): $150-800/month at the 'medium' tier.
Database Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17: $150-700/month.
cache: Azure Managed Redis in West Europe (Netherlands) $60-350/month.
queue: Azure Service Bus in West Europe (Netherlands) $5-30/month.
observability: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in West Europe (Netherlands) $30-200/month.
Stored data ~200 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average).
Spiky traffic: the upper bound is a peak month; with autoscaling, quiet months run near the lower bound.
Excluded: payment gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are a share of revenue, not infrastructure.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: p95 100 ms is achievable only with users near the Azure App Service (Linux, Premium v3, 2+ instances) region and no cross-region calls; the engine cannot measure it — load-test before launch.

GDPR: lawful basis and privacy notice, data-subject rights endpoints, DPAs with every processor (Art. 28), security of processing (Art. 32); transfers outside the EU need an adequacy decision or SCCs.
Upper estimate $2388/month can exceed the $1500 budget at peak usage.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'medium' from 50,000 users and ~5,000 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
gdpr with no data_residency: EU region (West Europe (Netherlands)) chosen to avoid international transfers.
